I recently posted a video about Sonder. Sonder is, according to The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows:

The realization that each random passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as your own—populated with their own ambitions, friends, routines, worries and inherited craziness—an epic story that continues invisibly around you like an anthill sprawling deep underground, with elaborate passageways to thousands of other lives that you’ll never know existed, in which you might appear only once, as an extra sipping coffee in the background, as a blur of traffic passing on the highway, as a lighted window at dusk.

Now, according to Webster's dictionary, sonder isn't a real word but, considering this subverse is dedicated to the absorption of the mind in fictional worlds, it makes no difference.

Now, I'd consider escapism to be the word that would best describe this subverse but, in a way, sonder would be a close second. Escapism is the avoidance of reality by absorption of the mind in entertainment or in an imaginative situation, activity, etc. The link between escapism and this subverse is apparent, but the link between sonder and this subverse is more subtle. The most typical case of sonder would be making eye contact with a passing stranger and realizing that that stranger has a life with as much complexity as yours. The cognitive bias that causes you to see yourself as the protagonist of your own life breaks down and you realize you're in a world full of people leading their own lives just as you do. These people have acquaintances, friends, memories, dreams, ambitions, and other things that make them unique, just like you do.

You're experiencing sonder just by navigating to this subverse because it's a construct of my own imagination. Each and every post you see in this subverse is sonder one way or another and likely in more ways than one. When somebody posts a picture of a person gazing off into the distance, it inspires wonder in the imagination of anybody who views said picture. This character gazing off into the sunset - what is he thinking? What inspired the artist to draw this? What inspired the poster to post this? What inspired the creation of this subverse? Just by looking at that picture, you're getting a glimpse into the minds of four different people and one of them isn't even real. You're getting a glimpse into the mind of the subject of the picture gazing off into the sunset, the artist, the poster, and myself. Whenever you explore a fictional world, in a way, you're not exploring a world at all but, more specifically, you're exploring someone else's mind.

I've already explained in a previous post why I do what I do here, but to add onto that, I created this place for the sake of adventure... for the sake of exploration. Sure, it's enthralling to gaze upon a picture of castles floating in the sky, airships, and mythical beasts, but what's possibly even more fascinating than that is the fact that there could be worlds like that in the imaginations of everyone you come across on a daily basis; each world unique and inspired by a long, complex chain of events that started from their very own day one.

The most fascinating thing one can explore is the mind of another human being.
